task_brief: Day 5 of "Capstone Review, Defense, and Transition" (unit 6, grade 12) is a second concept model on presentation in a chosen private or public mode. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 60–90 minutes. The unit is working toward: Defend the capstone in a chosen private or public mode with complete documentation, a response to independent review, and a maintenance and transition plan. Today's work contributes to that by handling presentation in a chosen private or public mode at the concept model b stage, against the unit's wider topics of evidence assembly and documentation, independent review and critique response, limitations and future work, and maintenance security and sunset planning. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Study the second model of presentation in a chosen private or public mode alongside the first one you traced earlier in this unit. Build a two-column comparison: what the two models do the same way, and where they diverge. Name the specific condition that decides which approach applies. Then take one input the first model handles well and hand-trace it through the second model, and explain in writing why the result matches or differs. Your comparison must cite a concrete step from each model, not a general impression of presentation in a chosen private or public mode. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about presentation in a chosen private or public mode, and it belongs to "Capstone Review, Defense, and Transition", which also covers separate topics such as evidence assembly and documentation. Close out with this check before you stop: State what the contrasting example of presentation in a chosen private or public mode revealed that the first one did not. At grade 12 the bar is portfolio-quality independent work you could defend to an outside reader: intent stated, method justified, limitations named honestly, and revision traceable.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.
Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, diagrammed, or demonstrated responses; where code is the target, accept pseudocode, block-based, or annotated-trace evidence.
Provide screen-reader-compatible editors, adjustable font and contrast, keyboard-only workflows, and an offline paper-and-trace route for every programming task.
task_accessibility_provisions: Provide a screen-reader-compatible editor, adjustable font size and contrast, and a complete keyboard-only workflow. An offline paper-and-trace route is available for every task here and is scored identically to an on-screen one.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Never use or require a real password, API key, access token, account credential, private message, precise location, or identifiable image; use clearly fictional placeholder values only.
Keep all security work in sandboxed, simulated, or fictional environments; never scan, probe, exploit, or attempt access against real systems, networks, accounts, services, or people.
Use approved sites and tools; do not bypass filters, access controls, licensing, or terms of service.
Treat AI output as a draft to verify and disclose. The tutor may explain concepts, ask diagnostic questions, and help debug, but never silently completes graded project work.

remediation: Reteaching for presentation in a chosen private or public mode follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for presentation in a chosen private or public mode, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to presentation in a chosen private or public mode works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of presentation in a chosen private or public mode, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking presentation in a chosen private or public mode mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply presentation in a chosen private or public mode under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on presentation in a chosen private or public mode rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
